scope: Primary-source BeatNet/madmom research and one non-held executable BeatNet diagnostic. This is not ARMv7 validation, transcription acceptance evidence, or a held-out evaluation.

beatnet.license: CC BY 4.0, repository LICENSE at the pinned revision

architecture.verified: BDA(272, 150, 2) uses Conv1d(1, 2, kernel_size=10), ReLU, max_pool1d(2), Linear(2*floor((272-10+1)/2), 150), a two-layer unidirectional LSTM with 150 cells, Linear(150, 3), and Softmax(dim=0).

weights.other_pinned_blobs: model-1/2/3.pt are 1614574 bytes each; model_1/2/3_weights.pt are 1612179 bytes each.

frontend.verified: Official BeatNet handler configures mono 22050 Hz audio, 1411-sample (64 ms) windows, 441-sample (20 ms) hops, a 24-band 30–17000 Hz filtered log spectrogram and positive spectral differences. The resulting input is 272 features at 50 fps.

decoder.defaults: 50 fps; 1500 beat particles; 250 downbeat particles; 55–215 BPM; 2–4 beats per bar.
decoder.limitation: The default bounds exclude the plan's 40 and 240 BPM fixtures. This diagnostic did not change those defaults.

madmom.pretrained_model_license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 according to the official madmom model repository/license records.
madmom.frontend: madmom RNNBeatProcessor source documents mono 44.1 kHz, 2048-sample STFT frames, 12-band 30–17000 Hz filtered log spectrograms and 100 fps activations.
madmom.restriction: CC BY-NC-SA requires attribution, non-commercial use, and share-alike. It does not itself prove that this user's standalone feature is prohibited; distribution/use terms need a product decision.

With seed 1 it emitted 86 beat/downbeat rows in 3.387 seconds; median interval 0.5 seconds (120 BPM).

armv7_path.candidate: Export the pinned BeatNet BDA activation network only, then retain an independently ported deterministic particle filter.
required_before_selection: Export state-dict model_1_weights.pt to an ARMv7-supported runtime and prove PyTorch-versus-target activation parity on frozen audio.
Implement or port the decoder without relying on a compiled madmom extension unavailable on the target.
Measure ARMv7 RAM, cold/warm latency, and 45-second capture processing.
Evaluate frozen 40–240 BPM, octave-error, phase, uncertainty and bar-start controls without changing the 55–215 default constraints during evaluation.
armv7_path.status: The x86 CPU diagnostic proves the pinned frontend and network can execute in split hosts. It does not establish ONNX conversion, ARMv7 support, timing, or required-range quality.

decision: BeatNet model 1 is a concrete CC-BY activation-model candidate for a separate ARM portability experiment. Its default decoder range and compiled madmom dependency remain material gaps. madmom pretrained RNN assets remain a comparison option subject to their CC BY-NC-SA terms, not an automatically excluded feature.

batch_executable_diagnostic.scope: Seven v10 acquisition fixtures only. All seven PCM hashes exactly match their corresponding v11 acquisition fixtures; none matched v11 development or held-out PCM. This is therefore not independent v11 or held-out evidence.
batch_executable_diagnostic.input_reference: Frozen v10 manifest BPM plus frozen recipe intro_seconds + record_phase_seconds; drift additionally uses its frozen 120-to-150 BPM transition at 22.5 seconds. Phase matching is monotonic one-to-one over every retained reference beat at <=50 ms.
batch_executable_diagnostic.model_loading: The upstream model=1 handler loads model_1_weights.pt SHA-256 619091bc317ca3e83b45591d46f6de3d5a41588bcb39fe9fe7be30cffa6aca84. The earlier 80e320... value is model-1.pt, a distinct upstream checkpoint blob that was not loaded.
batch_executable_diagnostic.default_55_215: 120 BPM: 86/86 matched (mean absolute phase error 4.05 ms). 180 BPM: 92/129 matched; 240 BPM: 62/172 matched and median output 120 BPM. 60 BPM produced a 120 BPM median with 43 extra predicted beats; 40 BPM produced 57 predictions for 29 references. Drift matched 84/102 but no uncertainty; the half/double ambiguous control emitted 85 beats and no uncertainty.
batch_executable_diagnostic.extended_40_240_dev_only: Predeclared separately, with no held-out tuning. It did not repair the edges: 40 BPM 20/29, 240 BPM 16/172, and it exposes no uncertainty result for drift or ambiguity. It is not an acceptance configuration.
batch_executable_diagnostic.timing: Pinned WSL particle-filter replay took 3.50–6.74 seconds per 45-second fixture/configuration; all 14 replay arrays were bit-for-bit equal to preserved outputs. Windows Torch CRNN inference was 0.234–0.297 seconds per 45-second fixture. No ARMv7 claim follows.

model23_executable_diagnostic.scope: Same frozen v10 acquisition frontend features as model 1; v10 bytes overlap corresponding v11 acquisition only, so this is not clean held-out evidence.

model2.default: 120 BPM 82/86 match, precision .976/recall .953; 180 43/129; 240 63/172. Drift 87/102 and correct local 120/150 median segments, but no uncertainty. Extended 40–240 gives a 40 BPM median but only 21/29 phase matches.

model3.default: 120 BPM 76/86; 180 10/129; 240 46/172. It estimates about 61.2 BPM on the ambiguous 60 BPM control, where models 1/2 estimate 120, but emits beats with precision .491/recall .600 rather than uncertainty.

model23_executable_diagnostic.candidate: Do not implement from this diagnostic. A future fail-closed three-model consensus could emit only when model grids agree within 2% tempo and >=90% bidirectional <=50ms phase correspondence, otherwise returning uncertain. It must inspect model outputs only, never fixture labels. It would expose model-3 disagreement on ambiguity, but all models can agree on the wrong 120 BPM octave at 60 BPM, so an independent confidence/tempo-hypothesis ambiguity test is required first.
model23_executable_diagnostic.uncertainty: All runs return timed beat/downbeat rows only. Drift and ambiguous controls cannot pass their required uncertainty behavior.
